name: Reconstructed boarding house on Lake Street, as Gifford draws it

grade.why: Placed by our reconstruction of the town; no source pictures or records it here.

documented_range.note: Drawn standing beside the first Tremont House (1833-1839) in Gifford's retrospective view of its street; taken as standing on 1 July 1835 on the owner's reading of the drawing (T-3605). No dated record of this building is known.

change_note: T-3605 builds this store as Gifford draws it.

placement.position_note: Placed in the drawn order along the face, at stations 1.50-16.70 m of the face line (The next block's Lake Street face, from the Clark corner west, on the same line as the row east of Clark.), with 0.30 m between neighbours. Drawn at x 200-318 px of the 1637 px plate. The face is the drawing's (read through the Tremont's solved camera, data/reconstruction/1835_gifford_street_faces.json camera); the station is fitted, not measured.
placement.symbolic_location: Lake Street, lake north west of clark: drawn store B of Gifford's row

footprint.note: 15.20 m of frontage proportioned from the drawn bays (gifford_tremont_house_no_1; the drawing's frontage stands over the H3 typology's own where the two differ), and 13.00 m deep, a depth the H3 typology allows. Neither is a measurement.

stories.note: READ OFF GIFFORD'S DRAWING of the first Tremont House and its street (gifford_tremont_house_no_1): a dark three-storey block standing up behind the low stores at the Clark end of the row, its flat-looking top and two stacks above them: read as the corner building across Clark. Graded reconstructed, not inferred: the value is the drawing's, but which building of 1835 the drawn front was is ours (the roof is an invented count-unit), the drawing is retrospective, and taking it as the street on 1 July 1835 is the owner's reading of 2026-11-15 (T-3605, docs/LIBERTIES.md L-gifford-street-faces-3605). The drawn value stands over the family's typology band where the two differ.

chimneys.note: INVENTED, NOT DERIVED. This value comes from a typology in the reconstruction spec — what a building of this kind was ordinarily like — and NOT from evidence about this particular building, because there is no particular building: the structure itself is an invention filling a demonstrable need of the town. The spec is cited because the invention is bounded by it, which is what makes it defensible rather than arbitrary; the GRADE is the bottom tier because nothing here is a reading of a source about this thing. Type-level choice within the H3 band in the supplied reconstruction specification; it is not evidence for this anonymous instance.

citations.citation: N. Roswell Gifford. View of the first Tremont House and the storefront row on its street — wash drawing, signed "N. Roswell Gifford" at the lower left. Reproduced on Chicagology, "Tremont House", captioned "Tremont House No. 1".
what_it_supplies: a continuous commercial frontage of one-and-a-half and two-storey stores standing shoulder to shoulder with shared party lines
a lettered signboard across the front of each store, some legible: H. WELLS, GROCERIES, BOOTS & SHOES, THOMPSON, & ALBEE
a raised board walk running the length of the frontage, with posts at the road edge
the first Tremont House as a three-storey shuttered block with a flagstaff, standing in the row rather than apart from it
gable-front and eaves-front stores alternating along one street rather than one repeated form
an unmade road of ruts and standing water in front of the row
what_it_does_not_supply: any coordinate, footprint outline or dimension — no scale, no baseline, no lettered street
which corner it is taken from: the caption names the building and not the viewpoint
awnings, which the brief lists and this plate does not legibly show
a date, either of the drawing or of the scene within the first Tremont's 1833-1839 life
the identity or trade of any store whose board is not legible

what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED FROM A PICTURE. Gifford draws this store in the row beside the first Tremont House; the owner ruled on 2026-11-15 that the drawing is a reasonable view of 1835 and the street is to be built to it. The drawn form is read off the drawing and graded reconstructed; the building's presence in July 1835, its exact frontage and its station are reconstructed. Its occupants, if any, are dealt by the town's housing tools and graded by their own records.

fabric_basis.words: whitewashed clapboard on a braced frame under a weather-darkened roof — a boarding house, from the 1832–33 town (rule F-B: a boarding-house or tavern keeper's by its type)

drawn.read: a dark three-storey block standing up behind the low stores at the Clark end of the row, its flat-looking top and two stacks above them: read as the corner building across Clark

lodging.note: Raised to a drawing of the street (the inventory's pictured_roofs, T-3605), not to house the town model's people, so the bed bracket does not count it and no beds are dealt here. Its rooms are recorded so a seating pass knows they exist.
